gloss: Hidden talents or powerful forces lying in wait.
teaser: Today, we uncover a phrase that speaks to hidden strengths and potential.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we uncover a phrase that speaks to hidden strengths and potential. [break 1s] The phrase is: 卧虎藏龙, wò hǔ cáng lóng. [break 1s] 卧 (wò) — to lie down [break 0.5s] 虎 (hǔ) — tiger [break 0.5s] 藏 (cáng) — to hide [break 0.5s] 龙 (lóng) — dragon [break 1s] So, the full idiom, 卧虎藏龙, literally means 'lying tiger hiding dragon,' and figuratively refers to hidden talents or powerful forces lying in wait. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a famous novel during the Ming Dynasty called 'The Knight-Errant.' It described a time when there were hidden heroes and talents not yet recognized. Just like a tiger that lies low and a dragon that hides, these figures could spring into action when the time was right. [break 1.5s] Now, for some examples: [break 1s] 在这个小镇上，卧虎藏龙，有很多隐秘的高手。 [break 1s] In this small town, there are hidden talents, many secret masters. [break 1s] 这位年轻的艺术家真是卧虎藏龙，作品令人惊叹。 [break 1s] This young artist is truly a hidden talent; their work is astonishing. [break 1s] 他看起来普通，但其实卧虎藏龙，能力非凡。 [break 1s] He seems ordinary, but in fact, he is a hidden talent with extraordinary abilities. [break 1s] So, remember, 卧虎藏龙 means 'hidden talents or powerful forces lying in wait.' Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.
